sources.citation: Stokhof, W.A.L. (ed.) 1982. Holle Lists: Vocabularies in languages of Indonesia, Vol. 5/1: Irian Jaya: Austronesian languages; Papuan languages, Digul area. PL D-52. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Contains no Iwur list (Glottolog's attachment is spurious): Digul-area lists are Awyu (Uwimerah, Mappi), Mandobo, Kaoh, Muyu (list 197) and a mixed Tanah Merah list 247 identified by the editors as Yonggom/South Kati (p. 175). Holle question-16 answers 'stress (placement) generally on the last syllable' appear for Digul Mappi p.140, Mandobo p.150, Kaoh p.161, Muyu p.173 -- none for Iwur.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C.L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1 (PL C-38), 345-459. Sec. 2.6.2.2.6.3.4 'Iwur', p. 383.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: 'Iwur is spoken on the south side of the central ranges in the valley of the Iwur River.. There are no language data available.' (p. 383). Only an intelligibility remark from Brongersma & Venema (Iwur understand Muyu, not Ngalum).

sources.citation: Healey, Alan. 1964. The Ok language family in New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University (hdl 1885/10871). Ch. I sec. 1.4, p. 44 (PDF p. 39).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Iwur: 'IWOER is the name tentatively given to the language of the people living in the valley of the Iwoer River.. The author has no sample of this language, and to his knowledge no one has studied it.' (p. 44). Tentatively grouped with Kati/Yonggom (Lowland Ok Division A).
